explanation: Petrarch's sonnets divide into eight lines and six. Shakespeare's run as three quatrains of four lines and end with a rhyming couplet that often turns the argument.

claims.text: A traditional sonnet does not have 10, 12 or 16 lines.
A Petrarchan sonnet divides into an octave of eight lines and a sestet of six.
A Shakespearean sonnet has three four-line quatrains followed by a rhyming couplet.
